Bug_Title: DMI: Invocation of hashCode on an array (DMI_INVOKING_HASHCODE_ON_ARRAY)
Bug_Details:
The code invokes hashCode on an array. Calling hashCode on
an array returns the same value as System.identityHashCode, and ignores
the contents and length of the array. If you need a hashCode that
depends on the contents of an array a,
use java.util.Arrays.hashCode(a).

 a java.util.Arrays.hashCode(a)
Bug_Explanation: The code invokes the hashCode method on an array object, which does not take into account the contents of the array. It returns the same value as System.identityHashCode, making it ineffective if the array's contents should influence the hashCode value.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug method in the JUnit test class calls the showBug method from the HashCodeDemo class twice with the same array, once before and once after modifying one element of the array. Since the bug is that hashCode() on an array does not consider the array's content, the hashCode values should be the same even if the array has been modified, which is incorrect behavior. The assertion assertEquals(hashCodeValue1, hashCodeValue2) is expected to fail if the bug is present, as the hash code should change when the array content changes.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that the test passed successfully without any assertion failures, which means the hashCode values were equal despite the array content change. This confirms that the bug was not triggered as the test did not demonstrate the expected failure.
